title: Editing & Error Correction
description: Master editing and error correction for Grade 9: grammar, lexical and structural errors, omission and passage editing in the CBSE/ICSE board format — bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Categories of Error
topics.concept:
Errors fall into a few predictable types — learn the list and check each one:

CategoryExample error → fix
TenseShe has went → has gone
Subject-verb agreementThe news are → is
ArticleShe is honest girl → an honest girl
PrepositionHe is good in maths → good at
PronounBetween you and I → you and me
Double negativeI don't know nothing → anything
Comparisonmore smarter → smarter
Redundancyreturn back → return

Structural errors include faulty parallelism and misplaced/dangling modifiers — covered in the next section.

examples.problem: Find and fix the error: He is more cleverer than his brother.
examples.solution: more cleverer → cleverer. Double comparatives are wrong.

examples.problem: Find and fix: I have been living here since five years.
examples.solution: since → for. Use 'for' with a length of time.

recap: Common error types: tense, agreement, article, preposition, pronoun
Also: double negatives, double comparatives, redundancy
Scan each line systematically in a fixed order

topics.title: Modifiers, Parallelism & Passage Editing
topics.concept:
Misplaced modifier: a describing word/phrase sits next to the wrong noun.

  • ❌ She almost drove the kids to school every day. → ✓ She drove the kids to school almost every day.

Dangling modifier: the opening phrase has no logical subject.

  • ❌ Walking to school, the rain started. → ✓ Walking to school, I felt the rain start.

Faulty parallelism: items in a list must share the same grammatical form.

  • ❌ She likes swimming, running, and to cycle. → ✓ swimming, running, and cycling.

Passage editing (CBSE format): each line has one error; write the wrong word and the correction. Omission exercises ask you to supply a missing word (often an article, preposition or helping verb).

examples.problem: Fix the parallelism: He is hardworking, honest, and a man of courage.
examples.solution: He is hardworking, honest, and courageous. — keep all items as adjectives.

examples.problem: Omission — supply the missing word: She is one of ___ best dancers.

recap: Keep a modifier next to the word it describes
An opening phrase must have a logical subject (no dangling)
List items must be parallel; passage editing = one error per line

questions.q: Correct: 'He have finished.'
Correct: 'She is good in singing.'
Correct: 'It is a honest mistake.'
Correct: 'The team are winning.' (acting as one)
Correct: 'He is more stronger.'
Correct: 'I don't know nothing.'
Supply the missing word: 'She is one ___ the best.'
Correct: 'We reached to the station.'
Correct: 'He has been ill since two days.'
Correct: 'Each students has a book.'
Correct: 'She suggested to go out.'
Correct: 'The childrens are playing.'
Find the error: 'Neither of the boys have done their homework.'
Edit: 'The scenery of the hills were breathtaking.'
Which correction fixes the misplaced modifier? 'He served sandwiches to the children on paper plates.'
options: He served sandwiches on paper plates to the children.
He served to the children sandwiches paper plates.
On paper plates he the children served sandwiches.
questions.explanation: The plates describe how the sandwiches were served, so the phrase belongs beside 'sandwiches'.

questions.q: Edit: 'Hardly had I reached the station when the train has left.'
questions.explanation: Both clauses are past; 'when the train left'.

questions.q: Find the error: 'The reason why he failed is because he was lazy.'
questions.explanation: 'The reason … is that …' — 'because' is redundant after 'the reason'.

questions.q: Edit: 'She is senior than me by two years.'
Supply the omitted word: 'He is not only clever ___ also kind.'
Fix the parallelism: 'The job requires patience, skill, and being honest.'
questions.explanation: Keep all items as nouns: patience, skill, honesty.

outcomes: Recognise the main categories of error
Correct tense, agreement, article and preposition errors
Spot misplaced and dangling modifiers and faulty parallelism

intro.en: Every board paper tests editing: a passage with one mistake in each line that you must find and fix. The secret is to scan systematically — check the verb, the subject-verb match, the article, the preposition, and the word choice. This chapter trains that editor's eye so errors jump out at you.
intro.hi: हर बोर्ड पेपर editing जाँचता है: एक अनुच्छेद जिसकी हर पंक्ति में एक गलती होती है, जिसे आपको ढूँढकर ठीक करना है। रहस्य है व्यवस्थित ढंग से देखना — क्रिया, कर्ता-क्रिया मेल, article, preposition और शब्द-चयन जाँचें। यह अध्याय वही संपादक-दृष्टि विकसित करता है ताकि गलतियाँ स्वयं उभर आएँ।

real_life.situation:
You proofread a friend's application:

Line: I am writing to apply for the post of librarian which was advertise in your newspaper.

Fix: …which was advertised in your newspaper.
real_life.why: One small slip — 'advertise' instead of 'advertised' — can spoil a formal letter. Editing is the skill of catching such errors before they cost you marks or credibility.

quick_test.q: 'Return back' is wrong because it is an example of:
quick_test.explanation: 'Return' already means 'go back', so 'return back' is redundant.

common_mistakes.note: Fix the agreement and the double negative.
Dangling modifier — give it a logical subject.

reading.passage:
Editing task — one error per line is shown with its correction:

Line 1: Yesterday I go to the market. (go → went)
Line 2: I buyed some fresh vegetables. (buyed → bought)
Line 3: The shopkeeper was very honest man. (was very → was a very)
Line 4: He gave me a discount because I am a regular customer. (am → was)

questions.q: Why is Line 1 corrected to 'went'?
questions.answer: 'Yesterday' signals a finished past action, which needs the simple past 'went'.

questions.q: What kind of error is 'buyed'?
questions.answer: A word-form (irregular verb) error — the past of 'buy' is 'bought'.

questions.q: What word is missing in Line 3?
questions.answer: The article 'a' — 'was a very honest man'.

speaking: He doesn't know anything about it.
She is better at maths than at science.
I have been here for two hours.
We discussed the plan in detail.
It is an honest and useful answer.

writing.prompt: Write a short paragraph (5 lines) that contains one deliberate error per line, then write the corrections beside each line — like a board editing exercise.
writing.example: Line: She go to school daily. (go → goes)

micro_quiz.q: Fix the error in 'I don't want no help':

options: She likes reading, writing and to paint.
micro_quiz.explanation: 'reading, writing and to paint' mixes forms; use 'painting'.

micro_quiz.q: Supply the missing word: 'It is ___ hour since he left.'

challenge.q: Fix the dangling modifier: 'Having finished the test, the bell rang.'
options: Having finished the test, we heard the bell ring.
Having finished the test, the bell was ringing.
The bell rang having finished the test.
Finishing the test the bell rang.
challenge.explanation: The doer of 'having finished' must be the subject ('we').

options: One of my friend is a doctor.
One of my friends is a doctor.
One of my friends are a doctor.
One of my friend are a doctor.
challenge.explanation: 'One of my friends is …' — plural noun, singular verb.

challenge.q: Identify the error: 'The teacher explained us the lesson.'

EDITING & ERROR CORRECTION
                |
   +--------+---+----+---------+
   |        |        |         |
 GRAMMAR  LEXICAL  STRUCTURAL FORMAT
 tense    wrong    misplaced  one error
 agreement word    dangling   per line
 article  prep     parallel   omission
 pronoun  redund.  modifier   (missing)
revision: Scan each line: verb/tense → agreement → article → preposition → word choice
Watch for double negatives, double comparatives and redundancy
Keep modifiers next to the word they describe; avoid dangling phrases
List items must be parallel (same grammatical form)
Passage editing = one error per line; omission = supply a missing word
